name: JSON Workbench
description: Format, validate, and query JSON in a live workbench.
longDescription: Pretty-prints, minifies, and validates JSON with line-and-column error reporting, plus a collapsible tree view, dot/bracket path queries, and document stats. Parsing happens in the browser, so nothing you paste is uploaded.

params.in: JSON text to parse and format

name: UUID Generator
description: Generate UUID v4 and v7 in bulk, and inspect existing UUIDs.
longDescription: Generates random v4 and time-ordered v7 UUIDs (RFC 9562) in bulk using the browser's crypto API, with a field-by-field anatomy view. Paste an existing UUID to read back its version, variant, and — for v7 — the embedded Unix timestamp.

params.in: a UUID to inspect (returns version, variant, and v7 timestamp)

name: Epoch Converter
description: Convert Unix timestamps to dates and back, across timezones.
longDescription: Converts Unix epoch timestamps in seconds or milliseconds to ISO 8601, UTC, local, and relative time, and turns a date back into a timestamp. Includes a running clock and a side-by-side multi-timezone view.

params.in: unix seconds/millis or a date string

name: Subnet Calculator
description: Work out network, broadcast, and host ranges from a CIDR block.
longDescription: Takes an IPv4 address and prefix and returns the network and broadcast addresses, subnet mask, wildcard mask, and usable host range, alongside an address-space map and a binary breakdown of the mask. The math runs in the browser.

name: Cron Builder
description: Build and explain cron expressions with a visual editor.
longDescription: Construct a schedule field by field, or paste an existing cron expression to read a plain-English description and a preview of the next run times. No backend involved.

name: Regex Tester
description: Test regular expressions with live match highlighting.
longDescription: Highlights matches as you type, lists captured groups, and lets you toggle flags. It uses the browser's own JavaScript regex engine, so what you see is what your JS code will do.

name: Permissions Auditor
description: Unix permissions: octal, symbolic, setuid, and risk flags.
longDescription: Converts between octal and symbolic Unix permissions with a read/write/execute grid that covers the setuid, setgid, and sticky bits. It also flags modes worth a second look, such as setuid combined with world-writable, or 0777.

params.in: octal (3-4 digit, e.g. 4755) or symbolic — a full string like rwxr-xr-x or chmod ops like u+x,go-w
params.type: optional: file | script | dir (tunes the security audit)
params.name: optional: filename used in the generated chmod command

name: Data Inspector
description: Decode Base64, hex, data-URIs, and JWTs, with a hex dump.
longDescription: Detects and decodes Base64, Base64URL, hex, data-URIs, and JWT segments, showing the decoded text next to a hex and ASCII dump with magic-byte guesses for PNG, GZIP, PDF, and ZIP. It encodes text or dropped files in the same formats too, all in the page.

name: Password Generator
description: Passwords and diceware passphrases with an entropy readout.
longDescription: Generates random passwords and diceware passphrases with the Web Crypto API, with controls for length, character sets, word count, and separators. The meter reports entropy in bits and an estimated offline cracking time — an estimate that depends on assumptions about the attacker.

params.sep: passphrase separator: dash/dot/space/under/digit or a literal char

name: Hash Generator
description: Generate SHA-256, SHA-512, SHA-1, and MD5 hashes.
longDescription: Hashes text or files locally. SHA-256, SHA-512, and SHA-1 use Web Crypto; MD5 uses a local legacy JavaScript implementation. Files are read locally rather than uploaded. SHA-1 and MD5 are here for checksum compatibility, not for security work.

name: JWT Decoder
description: Decode JWT headers, payloads, and claims.
longDescription: Decodes the header and payload of a JSON Web Token and lays out its claims, including issued-at and expiry times. It does not verify the signature, so a token that decodes cleanly is not necessarily a valid one.

name: Color Converter
description: Convert colors between HEX, RGB, HSL, and HSV.
longDescription: Converts a color between HEX, RGB, HSL, and HSV with a live swatch, so a value can move between CSS, design tokens, and an image editor without a round trip.

name: URL Encoder
description: Percent-encode, decode, and inspect URLs and query strings.
longDescription: Encodes and decodes strings using encodeURIComponent or encodeURI semantics, and splits a URL or query string into a table of percent-decoded parameters. Everything runs in the page.

name: cURL Converter
description: Convert cURL commands to Python, JavaScript, Go, or Bash.
longDescription: Parses a curl command's method, headers, data, and auth flags and writes the equivalent Python requests, JavaScript fetch, Go net/http, or wget code. Unusual flags may not translate cleanly, so read the output before running it.

name: Dockerfile Optimizer
description: Review Dockerfiles for layer caching and common pitfalls.
longDescription: Reads a Dockerfile and points out layer ordering that busts the build cache, unpinned versions, missing ignore patterns, and steps that inflate image size. The suggestions are heuristics — apply the ones that fit your build.

name: Secret Vault
description: Encrypt and decrypt text or files with a passphrase.
longDescription: Encrypts text or files with AES-256-GCM, deriving the key from your passphrase using PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 at 600,000 iterations (the current OWASP figure). The output blob carries its own salt, IV, and derivation parameters, so anyone with the passphrase can decrypt it on this page later.
privacyNote: Encryption and decryption happen in your browser using the Web Crypto API. The passphrase is never stored and the tool makes no network requests — the ciphertext only goes wherever you choose to send it.

name: One-Time Secret
description: Share a secret through an expiring, best-effort burn-after-read link.
longDescription: Stores a secret in Cloudflare KV and returns an unguessable retrieval link. The worker requests deletion after a successful read, but KV is eventually consistent, so this is not a guaranteed one-read channel. The secret travels to infrastructure we operate; encrypt it locally with Secret Lock first if the operator must not be able to read it.
privacyNote: This is not end-to-end encrypted: the secret is sent to an edge worker and stored in eventually consistent KV until expiry or a deletion request after retrieval. Concurrent or geographically separated reads may succeed more than once. The worker operator could read the value; use browser-local Secret Lock first when that is unacceptable.

name: Secrets Scanner
description: Scan pasted code and config for exposed keys and tokens.
longDescription: Matches pasted code or config against patterns for AWS keys, GitHub tokens, private keys, connection strings, and other credential shapes, reporting hits with line numbers. Pattern matching produces both false positives and misses, so treat the output as a prompt to look, not a clean bill of health.

name: Security Headers Analyzer
description: Grade pasted HTTP response headers and suggest fixes.
longDescription: Reads a block of HTTP response headers, scores what is present or missing across CSP, HSTS, X-Frame-Options, and related headers, and offers corrected values to paste into your server config. The grade reflects the headers you supply, not how the site actually behaves.

name: CSP Generator
description: Build Content-Security-Policy headers directive by directive.
longDescription: Toggle directives and add allowed sources to assemble a Content-Security-Policy, with the finished header string and its meta-tag equivalent updating as you go. Test any policy against your real pages before shipping it.

name: DMARC / SPF / DKIM Builder
description: Generate email auth records with plain-English explanations.
longDescription: A guided form for DMARC, SPF, and DKIM DNS records that explains what each tag does and emits copy-ready TXT values. Roll DMARC out in monitoring mode and read the reports before moving to enforcement.

name: TOTP Generator
description: Generate time-based one-time passwords from a Base32 secret.
longDescription: Computes RFC 6238 TOTP codes from a Base32 secret with a countdown to the next window, matching what an authenticator app would show. Computation happens in the browser, which makes it handy for testing enrollment flows.

name: SSH Key Generator
description: Generate Ed25519 and RSA SSH keypairs in your browser.
longDescription: Generates Ed25519 and RSA key pairs with the Web Crypto API and exports the public key in OpenSSH format and the private key as OpenSSH or PKCS#8 PEM, along with the SHA-256 fingerprint and randomart. Keys are created in the page and not uploaded.

name: .gitignore Generator
description: Build a .gitignore from languages, frameworks, and editors.
longDescription: Pick the languages, frameworks, editors, and operating systems you use and get one merged .gitignore drawn from the standard templates plus the usual editor and OS patterns.

name: Nginx Config Generator
description: Generate Nginx server blocks for proxying, SSL, and redirects.
longDescription: Produces commented Nginx server block configs for reverse proxying, SSL termination, static sites, HTTP-to-HTTPS redirects, and rate limiting. Check the output against your own Nginx version before deploying it.

name: GitHub Actions Generator
description: Compose GitHub Actions workflows with a visual builder.
longDescription: Choose a language, test runner, build steps, and deploy target to assemble a .github/workflows YAML file you can commit. Treat it as a starting point — pin action versions and review secrets before it runs.

name: Kubernetes Manifest Generator
description: Generate Deployment, Service, Ingress, and ConfigMap YAML.
longDescription: Fill in a form to produce Kubernetes Deployment, Service, Ingress, ConfigMap, and HPA manifests with resource requests and limits, liveness and readiness probes, and common annotations already wired in.

name: JSON to TypeScript
description: Generate TypeScript interfaces from a JSON sample.
longDescription: Infers TypeScript interfaces or type aliases from a pasted JSON object or array, handling nesting, arrays, and unions. The types reflect the sample you paste, so fields missing from it will not appear.

name: API Request Builder
description: Build and send HTTP requests from the browser.
longDescription: Set a method, URL, headers, query params, and body, send the request from your browser, and read back the status, response headers, and formatted JSON. Cross-origin calls are subject to the target's CORS policy.
privacyNote: This sends the request you compose from your browser directly to the URL you enter. Anything you put in it — headers, tokens, body — goes to that server. It is not routed through us, and we don't see it.

name: CSS Grid Generator
description: Lay out CSS Grid and Flexbox visually and copy the CSS.
longDescription: Set columns, rows, gaps, and alignment by dragging, and read the generated CSS Grid or Flexbox rules — grid-template-areas included — as the layout changes.

name: Meta Tag Generator
description: Generate Open Graph, Twitter Card, and SEO meta tags.
longDescription: Fill in a title, description, image, and URL to get Open Graph, Twitter Card, and SEO tags beside a mock share card. Tag generation is local; if you enter an image URL, the browser loads that image directly from its host for the preview.
privacyNote: Text and tag generation stay in the page. Entering an OG image URL makes the browser request that image directly from its host, which receives ordinary request and network metadata.

name: SVG Optimizer
description: Minify SVGs by stripping metadata and redundant markup.
longDescription: Removes editor metadata, collapses groups, converts basic shapes to paths, and drops invisible elements, reporting the before-and-after byte count. How much it saves depends entirely on the source file, so check the preview for visual changes.

name: Diff Viewer
description: Compare two blocks of text side by side.
longDescription: Shows added, removed, and changed lines between two texts in either side-by-side or unified view, with word-level highlighting inside the changed lines.

name: Word & Character Counter
description: Count words, characters, sentences, and reading time.
longDescription: Counts words, characters, sentences, and paragraphs as you type, with reading and speaking time derived from average rates. Handy for drafts with a length limit.

name: CSV ↔ JSON Converter
description: Convert between CSV and JSON with a table preview.
longDescription: Converts CSV to JSON and back, handling header rows and quoted fields, with an interactive table so you can check the parse before copying the result.

name: .env File Linter
description: Check .env files for duplicates, empty values, and secrets.
longDescription: Reads a .env file and reports duplicate keys, empty values, stray whitespace, unquoted special characters, and values that look like live credentials, line by line with suggested fixes.

name: DNS Record Builder
description: Build and explain A, AAAA, CNAME, MX, TXT, SRV, and CAA records.
longDescription: Builds and validates DNS records across the common types — A, AAAA, CNAME, MX, TXT, SRV, NS, and CAA — explaining each field in plain language and emitting zone-file lines to paste into your provider.

name: IP & Network Toolkit
description: Public IP display, address details, and IPv4 CIDR overlap checks.
longDescription: Fetches your public IP from api.ipify.org (with an httpbin fallback), shows local address representations and classification, and checks IPv4 CIDR overlap in the browser. It does not perform ASN or geolocation lookup.
privacyNote: The CIDR and subnet math runs in your browser. The public-IP lookup is the exception: it calls a third-party service (api.ipify.org), which necessarily sees the address it reports back to you.

name: Log Parser & Highlighter
description: Detect log formats, highlight syntax, and filter by level.
longDescription: Works out whether pasted output is JSON, Apache, nginx, syslog, or plain text, then highlights the fields, filters by log level, and sorts by timestamp. Format detection is a guess; unfamiliar formats fall back to plain text.

name: Breach Checker
description: Check a password against breach corpora using k-anonymity.
longDescription: Hashes your input with SHA-1 in the browser and sends only the first five characters of that hash to the Have I Been Pwned range API, so the secret itself is never transmitted. No match means it is absent from that corpus — not that it is a good password.
privacyNote: Your password is hashed in your browser, and only the first five characters of that hash are sent to the Have I Been Pwned range API. The service never receives the password or the full hash, and it can't tell which of the returned matches was yours.

name: IR Timeline Builder
description: Build incident timelines and export them to JSON or CSV.
longDescription: Add timestamped events with severity and notes to assemble an incident response timeline, then export it as JSON or CSV for the write-up. Entries live in your browser's local storage, so clearing site data removes them.

name: Site Score
description: Check a URL against a fixed list of HTTP response headers.
longDescription: Fetches a URL through our edge worker and grades a fixed list of HTTP response headers such as HSTS, CSP, and Referrer-Policy. It does not inspect certificates, TLS protocol configuration, page content, or overall application security; the result is a limited header checklist.
privacyNote: The URL you enter is sent to an edge worker we run. The worker fetches it and returns response headers, status, and final URL; it does not read the response body for this check.

name: Header Analyzer
description: Paste raw HTTP headers for a plain-English breakdown.
longDescription: Takes response headers copied from curl or DevTools and explains what each security-relevant header does and where a value is weak. Since you supply the headers, it works for localhost, staging, and captured traffic.

name: .env Exposure Analyzer
description: Identify secret types in a .env and what each one unlocks.
longDescription: Classifies the credentials in a pasted .env by service, describes what a leaked key of that type would give access to, and lays out the rotation steps for that provider. Classification is pattern-based, so unusual key formats may go unrecognized.

name: Privacy Scan
description: Check fetched HTML for bundled tracker and fingerprinting-related patterns.
longDescription: Fetches one page through our edge worker and searches its static HTML, response cookies, and referenced domains for a bundled set of tracker names and fingerprinting-related API strings. It does not execute scripts or prove runtime collection; ordinary API uses can match and later, authenticated, consent-gated, or interactive behavior is out of scope.
privacyNote: The URL you enter is sent to an edge worker we run, which fetches up to 2 MB of static HTML plus response headers and returns heuristic matches. The scan does not execute the page.

name: CT Monitor
description: Search Certificate Transparency logs for a domain's certificates.
longDescription: Queries crt.sh through our worker for certificate records matching an entered domain and its subdomains, returning up to 100 recent unique rows. It can help review unexpected issuance, but does not search typo or look-alike sibling domains; results inherit crt.sh coverage, ordering, and indexing lag.
privacyNote: The domain you enter is sent to an edge worker we run, which queries public Certificate Transparency logs and returns the matches.

name: ReDoS Tester
description: Check regexes for catastrophic backtracking.
longDescription: Looks for nested quantifiers and overlapping alternations that let a regex blow up on crafted input, then times the pattern against generated attack strings to show the effect. Analysis of this kind flags likely problems; it cannot prove a pattern is safe.

name: JWT Attack Workbench
description: Inspect JWTs for alg confusion, alg:none, and weak claims.
longDescription: Decodes a token and checks it against known JWT weaknesses — the alg:none bypass (CVE-2015-9235), RS256-to-HS256 confusion, missing or overlong expiry, and sensitive data in the payload — and can forge modified tokens for systems you are authorized to test. The findings describe the token; whether a server is actually vulnerable depends on how it verifies.

name: IOC Workbench
description: Extract, defang, and export indicators from any text.
longDescription: Pulls IPs, domains, URLs, file hashes, CVEs, and MITRE ATT&CK technique IDs out of pasted reports or logs, defangs them for safe sharing, and exports to CSV, JSON, STIX, or markdown. Extraction is regex-based, so review the list before it goes into a case file.

name: Prompt Defense Checklist
description: Check an LLM system prompt for configured defense-language patterns.
longDescription: Matches a pasted system prompt against configured defense-language patterns associated with ten injection categories. Bundled injection shapes are shown only as review context; they are not executed against a model. The score reports phrase coverage, not whether a model will resist or succumb to injection.

name: SIEM Query Translator
description: Translate detection queries between SPL, KQL, ES|QL, and Sigma.
longDescription: Converts a detection query between Splunk SPL, Microsoft Sentinel KQL, Elastic ES|QL, Sigma YAML, and Sumo Logic, with field mapping and notes on what did not carry over. These languages do not map one-to-one — test the output against your own data.

name: Email Header Forensics
description: Read email headers for routing, auth results, and phishing signs.
longDescription: Parses raw email headers into a hop-by-hop timeline with delivery delays, surfaces the SPF, DKIM, and DMARC verdicts the receiving server recorded, and scores common phishing indicators. Upstream headers can be forged, so weight the ones your own mail server added most heavily.

name: AI Cost Calculator
description: Compare LLM API prices across providers for a given workload.
longDescription: Estimates and compares API costs for models from Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Mistral, and open-weight/self-hosted options, from token counts or pasted text, broken down by input and output. Pricing comes from a static table last updated March 2026 — check the provider's page before you budget against it.

name: PII & Secrets Redactor
description: Redact PII and secrets from logs with stable pseudonyms.
longDescription: Finds emails, phone numbers, SSNs, card numbers, API keys, and connection strings in pasted logs or configs and replaces each with a stable pseudonym, so you can still correlate lines after redaction. Detection is pattern-based — read the result before sharing it.

name: CORS Debugger
description: Explain a CORS failure and generate the config to fix it.
longDescription: Describe your origin, target, method, and headers to get a plain-English account of why the browser is blocking the request, the preflight it would send, and copy-ready CORS config for Express, nginx, Cloudflare Workers, Flask, AWS API Gateway, or Apache.

name: WAF Rule Builder
description: Test a detection regex and export it as a WAF rule.
longDescription: Runs your regex against 110+ sample attack payloads across six categories — XSS, SQLi, path traversal, command injection and more — plus benign strings to surface false positives, then exports the pattern as a Cloudflare, AWS WAF, ModSecurity, nginx, or Apache rule. The payload set is a smoke test, not coverage.

name: Agent Security Audit
description: Review AI agent tool definitions for risky permissions.
longDescription: Reads MCP server definitions, function-calling schemas, or agent tool configs and points out over-broad permissions, untrusted input reaching the model, plausible exfiltration paths, and tool combinations that are risky together. It reasons about the config you paste, not the running agent.

name: SSL Chain Debugger
description: Parse a PEM chain, spot ordering problems, and reorder it.
longDescription: Parses pasted PEM certificates into a chain diagram, checks expiry, key strength, and issuer links, and reorders the chain when the pieces are out of sequence or an intermediate is missing. It also prints the openssl commands to check the same things against a live host.

name: Container Security Linter
description: Lint Kubernetes YAML, Dockerfiles, and compose for misconfigs.
longDescription: Checks Kubernetes manifests, Dockerfiles, and docker-compose files against rules for running as root, privileged containers, missing resource limits, hard-coded secrets, and similar issues, and offers a corrected version. Rule-based linting catches the patterns it knows about.

name: LLM Privacy Analyzer
description: Check an LLM API request for PII before you send it.
longDescription: Scans an OpenAI, Anthropic, or Google-format request body for emails, SSNs, card numbers, API keys, and other sensitive strings sitting in the prompt. The scan runs in your browser — shipping a privacy checker's input to a server would defeat the point — and pattern matching will miss some things.

name: Email Auth Wizard
description: Build SPF, DKIM, and DMARC records with a guided wizard.
longDescription: Walks through your sending providers, policy choices, and reporting addresses to produce SPF, DKIM, and DMARC TXT records with explanations and per-provider deployment notes. Start DMARC at p=none and read the reports before tightening it.

name: YARA Playground
description: Write and test YARA rules with templates and syntax checks.
longDescription: A YARA rule editor with syntax validation, starter templates for malware families, webshells, packers, and miners, a hex string builder, and notes on constructs that scan slowly. In-browser matching is approximate — validate rules with the real YARA engine before deploying them.

name: Sigma Rule Builder
description: Build Sigma detection rules with live YAML and SIEM export.
longDescription: A guided form for Sigma rules — logsource, detection logic with field modifiers, MITRE ATT&CK tags, and metadata — with live YAML preview and export to Splunk SPL, KQL, or ES|QL. Backend conversion is approximate; run the query in your SIEM before trusting it.

name: AI Model Scanner
description: Check model cards and configs for supply-chain red flags.
longDescription: Reads a HuggingFace model card, config.json, or requirements.txt and flags pickle-based weights, trust_remote_code, vulnerable pinned dependencies, and missing license or safety metadata. It reads the metadata you paste, not the weights, so a clean report is not evidence the model is safe.

name: Passkey Inspector
description: Decode WebAuthn attestation, authenticator data, and COSE keys.
longDescription: Paste an existing attestation object to decode its CBOR, authenticator flags, AAGUID, credential ID, and COSE key locally. Optional live-create mode asks the authenticator or password manager to create a real penumbraforge.com credential, which it may retain or sync; returned registration data is not submitted to an application server.

name: Entropy X-ray
description: Spot encrypted, compressed, or packed data by byte entropy.
longDescription: Plots Shannon entropy across a file offset by offset alongside a byte histogram, which is how packed or encrypted regions and embedded keys tend to stand out from code and text. High entropy is a hint about structure, not a verdict — confirm by looking at the bytes.

name: Key Converter
description: Convert keys between JWK and PEM, and generate RSA/EC pairs.
longDescription: Converts keys between JWK and PEM (SPKI and PKCS#8), generates fresh RSA and EC key pairs, and shows the underlying key parameters, all through the browser's Web Crypto API. Nothing is uploaded.

name: Local Chat
description: Chat with a small model in your browser, or your own server.
longDescription: Runs a small quantized model in the browser over WebGPU, or sends conversations to an OpenAI-compatible endpoint you configure. In-browser models are useful for quick questions rather than frontier quality. The selected engine determines whether conversation text stays in the page or goes to an endpoint.

name: Chat with your files
description: Ask questions over your own documents, in the browser.
longDescription: Chunks text, markdown, CSV, log, and source files in the browser, retrieves passages by embedding similarity, and answers with citations. WebGPU mode keeps processing in-page; configured endpoint modes send text chunks and questions to that endpoint. Check the cited passages and the selected route.

name: Regex from English
description: Describe a pattern in plain English, get a regex to test.
longDescription: A selected AI engine turns your description into a regular expression for JavaScript, PCRE, or Python, which you then test against sample text on the page; it can also explain a regex you paste. WebGPU stays in-page, while endpoint modes send the prompt to the configured URL. Generated patterns are drafts.

name: Command Explainer
description: Explain a shell command and flag dangerous parts first.
longDescription: Breaks a shell, git, docker, or kubectl command into its parts with a selected AI engine, and runs a separate browser-local rule scan for known destructive patterns. WebGPU keeps the command in-page; endpoint modes send it to the configured URL. Read the command yourself before running it.

name: AI Security Copilot
description: Paste a header, JWT, cert, or config for a local risk read.
longDescription: Decodes JWTs, inventories HTTP security headers, parses X.509 certificates, audits CSP directives, and scans configs for secrets with browser-local parsers, then asks the selected AI engine to summarize. Endpoint modes send the relevant input and findings to the configured URL. Treat model commentary as a draft.

name: EXIF Viewer & Scrubber
description: See the GPS and camera data in your photos, then strip it.
longDescription: Reads the EXIF tags, GPS coordinates, timestamps, and PNG text chunks embedded in JPEG, PNG, and WebP files, then writes out a copy with them removed. Images are decoded in the browser, so the location and device details never leave your machine.

name: Image Converter & Compressor
description: Convert and compress PNG, JPEG, and WebP in batches.
longDescription: Converts between PNG, JPEG, and WebP with a quality slider, aspect-preserving resize, and a before/after preview showing the byte difference. Encoding uses the browser's canvas, so the files stay on your device.

name: Color Contrast Lab
description: Check WCAG 2.1 and APCA contrast, with fixes for failures.
longDescription: Reports WCAG 2.1 contrast ratios and APCA Lc scores for a text and background pair, shows AA/AAA pass-fail at each text size, and nudges failing colors to the nearest passing value. Includes a tonal palette generator built on the same checks.

name: Open Graph Image Studio
description: Design 1200×630 social cards and export a PNG.
longDescription: Lays out Open Graph and Twitter card images at the 1200×630 size the platforms crop to, with presets, gradient and mesh backgrounds, and logo or emoji support. The card renders on a canvas in your browser and downloads as a PNG.

name: Favicon & PWA Asset Generator
description: Generate favicon and PWA icons from an image, emoji, or monogram.
longDescription: Produces 16, 32, 48, 180, 192, and 512 pixel PNGs, a multi-resolution favicon.ico, the matching HTML link tags, and a site.webmanifest from a single source image, emoji, or monogram. Rendering happens in the browser.
